calibration.assessmentStateNote: COMPUTED_VERIFIED as of R-2, and the road here is worth stating because two of its three steps were corrections of this control's own record. B-2 left the blocker as 'rottay's DB door lowers ZERO of the declared channels'. R-1 measured that claim FALSE -- the door lowers nineteen variables into modeDeltas[light], two of them declared -- and the refusal came from an INSTRUMENT guard that read only the base map (ROTTAY_DB_SEED_LANDS_IN_THE_NON_DEFAULT_MODE). R-2 widened both guards of that era to the union of every scope, gave the DB document a declared mode scope read fail-closed from the published BrandTheme, and re-ran everything: rottay went from 'the harness refuses the run, there is no arm' to an arm that reads identically to the static one, with zero divergent rows, for the stops its own contrast floor admits and in its own default mode -- the bounded claim written in calibration.equivalenceClaimScope, not a general statement about the two doors. The DT ruling of 2026-08-24 approved the per-vertical stop roster the contrast floor forces (calibration.stopAdmissibilityByVertical), so the declared domain is carried measured rather than quietly narrowed. calibration.evidenceKindLabellingRule: SIX RECEIPTS, TWO KINDS, SPLIT BY THE PROOF EACH RUN CARRIES -- the same convention density.mode uses. Each vertical's FIRST admissible stop carries static-db-computed-parity (the two doors compiled and painted the same result on one DOM: rottay/warm-sand, bithire/crimson, evnto/crimson) and its SECOND carries exact-restore (every applied variable returned to its pre-mutation reading: rottay/pale-mint, bithire/indigo, evnto/indigo). Both properties hold in all six runs; the labels say which one each receipt is cited FOR, not which one it measured. THE PRE-R-2 ARTIFACTS ARE NOT RECEIPTED AND MUST NOT BE: the {evnto-crimson,evnto-indigo}.MEASURED-NOT-RECEIPTED.json and the five B2-*.MEASURED-NOT-RECEIPTED.json files were produced by instrument bytes that no longer exist, so a receipt over them would attest sources that did not produce them (W-B). They stand as historical evidence, cited by measuredResult.b2StaticAuthorship and nothing else.
calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: Three, at every-measured-target scope. "color remains fixed" is deliberately absent: it is what this control MOVES. The three that remain — type, stroke, motion — are orthogonal to a colour seed and held in every scenario measured, on both arms.
calibration.stopSemantics: A STOP IS A (ROLE, HEX) PAIR: the mutation of ONE role, not of the palette. Measured: each of primaryColor / secondaryColor / accentColor moves exactly its own ten ramp steps and crosses ZERO into another role, which is what makes the per-role negative decidable with an exact zero instead of a tolerance. The alternatives were refuted by absence, not by preference: no preset palette catalog exists anywhere in src (and that shape already has its own domain kind, profile-id, with its calibration.catalog law), and no hue-rotation mechanism exists (the ramp holds hue constant by design). An IDENTITY stop declares no value and resolves against the arm's own baseline: it is the first identity in this programme that differs per vertical (#FFFFFF / #3A6FB0 / #171717), and it fails closed rather than inventing one.

measuredResult.instrument: packages/core/src/tooling/resolution-probe, Chromium, --bundle fresh, Node 22.17.0, plus direct compiles through the productive doors for step 0 and the identity law.
measuredResult.step0Apca: RUN FIRST, BEFORE ANY STOP WAS AUTHORED, and it disqualified an axis. Every background candidate THROWS TenantThemeValidationError on the DB arm in 3/3 verticals: #123456 and #0B0B0C leave --ds-color-text-primary at APCA Lc 0.0 against the new ground, #F7F7F5 leaves --ds-color-text-muted/-disabled below the floor (Lc 48.2 / 50.2 / 36.2). measuredResult.perRoleIsolation: Measured on deriveTenantColorRamps over a fixed 7-seed palette: primaryColor, secondaryColor and accentColor each move exactly 10 channels — their own role's ten steps — and 0 channels of any other role. backgroundColor moves 63 of 70: nine of ten steps in ALL SEVEN roles, including success/warning/error/info, which this control does not seed. The ground is the ramp ground, not a fourth peer seed. Drilled (F4B-8 drills 5 and 6).
measuredResult.identityLaw: W-A, measured on both arms. STATIC: writing the vertical's own value at the role keypath moves ZERO channels — 3 roles x 3 verticals, nine cases, all zero. The identity law holds exactly. DB: it does NOT — writing the vertical's own colour still emits a non-empty delta (bithire 7 vars, evnto 5, the same count for all three roles, so it is colour-independent), and rottay/primary (#FFFFFF) even throws on APCA. The DB arm takes no baseline by law (H-1 V5), so an identity stop is a STATIC-ARM claim; the harness refuses it on the DB arm rather than inventing the vertical value there.
measuredResult.invalidSeedIsSilent: THE FALSE GREEN THIS CONTROL BRINGS, measured not theorised. A non-hex seed does not throw and does not produce NaN: hexToRgbFloat runs parseInt(value, 16), NaN >> 16 & 255 is 0 in JS, so the seed becomes BLACK and derives a plausible GREY ramp. rebeccapurple and rgb(59, 130, 246) — both valid CSS colours — collapse this way. The channel MOVES, so a probe asking "did it move?" certifies as live a control that discarded the tenant colour. The signature that betrays it: --ds-color-primary passes the raw string through, the ramp goes achromatic, and --ds-chart-series-1 DISAPPEARS (it is behind isHexColor; the ramp derivation is not). The color-set branch refuses non-hex for exactly this reason (drill 3).

Both stops give identical divergence counts, so the divergence is a property of the axis, not of the colour.

measuredResult.r2GuardWidening: R-2, MEASURED 2026-08-24. The refusal that blocked this control for three packets was an INSTRUMENT defect with two sites of the same era, both now widened. (i) lowerStop's empty-lowering guard stood between the base-map extraction and the mode extraction H-3 phase (a) added 35 lines below it, so it asked 'is the base map empty?' while claiming to answer 'did the door lower anything?'. It now sits below the mode extraction and is computed over the UNION of every scope the compiler wrote; the message names the scopes it found. (ii) assertVariables, used by composeStaticArm/composeDbArm, had the same shape and accepts an empty base map when a mode block is non-empty. PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL UNIT, not by reading: lowerStop was driven with the exact shape compileTenantThemeConfig returns for rottay/crimson (variables {}, modeDeltas [light: 19]) and it threw the recorded message verbatim before the change and composes an arm after it (R-2 drills 1 and 2). THE WIDENING IS MONOTONE and that is what protects the 46: the new law only ADMITS lowerings the old one refused, so an arm with a non-empty base map -- which every receipted arm has -- takes the identical path and yields byte-identical variables (R-2 drill 7).
measuredResult.r2ScopeMatchedDoor: R-2, MEASURED. The probe's DB document now declares palette.backgroundMode = the vertical's own defaultMode, read fail-closed from the PUBLISHED BrandTheme via loadStaticBaselines() under the same freshness law the compilers use. Result on all three verticals: the DB seed lands in the BASE map at the same value the static arm writes, so the parity run compares one question instead of two (R-2 drill 6, which asserts the two arms agree on --ds-color-primary for every admissible stop). W-A ASKED FOR THE SOURCE TO BE VERIFIED AND THE VERIFICATION CORRECTED ITS EVIDENCE: the preaudit's reason was that FIRST_PARTY_THEMES.<v>.appearance.defaultMode is undefined; measured, it is 'dark' -- the Theme projection DOES carry the field. The prescription is right for a stronger reason, now asserted in the drill: FIRST_PARTY_THEMES is not exported from the published entrypoint at all, so reaching it would require the deep import this harness refuses for its compilers, while <vertical>BrandTheme is published and already loaded.
measuredResult.r2H2Decidability: R-2, MEASURED per arm per vertical against the real compilers, which is the STOP the brief named. DB arm: rottay lowers primary/warm-sand and primary/pale-mint (2 witnesses) and excludes crimson/indigo/identity; bithire and evnto lower primary/crimson and primary/indigo (2 witnesses) and exclude warm-sand/pale-mint/identity. STATIC arm: all four colour stops lower on all three verticals (4 witnesses), because compileBrandTheme applies no contrast floor. In all six arm x vertical combinations the verdict is PASS and --ds-color-primary is among the discriminating channels. The excluded stops are published with their reason by the guard itself, which is the existing legitimate class ('the vertical envelope rejects the stop', as for radius/recto and effect/estandar).
measuredResult.r2BlindWitnesses: THREE OF THE FIVE DECLARED CHANNELS CANNOT WITNESS THIS CONTROL ON SOME VERTICAL, each for a different and measured reason. (i) --ds-color-primary-500 is INERT on rottay: rottay is the only vertical that authors palette.ramps.primary in its body (all ten steps; bithire and evnto author none), and authored steps win over derivation (brand-theme/index.ts:358-366). (ii) --ds-button-primary-bg is STRUCTURALLY BLIND on rottay and evnto: both author the alias var(--ds-color-primary) as the leaf, and an alias's TEXT is constant across stops, so the channel never appears in a delta even though what it resolves to does move. bithire authors the literal #3A6FB0, which is why it is the one vertical where B-2's authorship change made this channel move. (iii) --ds-color-text-on-primary is INERT on all three: every vertical authors palette.onPrimaryColor explicitly (#0C0C0E on rottay, #ffffff on bithire and evnto), and an authored leaf is not re-derived from the seed. So the two reliable witnesses are --ds-color-primary (assigned straight from the seed, brand-theme:825) and --ds-chart-series-1 (derived from it). Two is enough for H-2, and the three blind ones are declared rather than quietly dropped.
measuredResult.r2CausalRuns: SIX CAUSAL RUNS, R-2, Chromium, --bundle fresh, Node 22.17.0, full fixture roster, source digest declared and matched on every run. ALL SIX: self-check=harness-live, pass=true, ingress equivalence IDENTICAL with ZERO differing rows, restore exact everywhere, negative controls held. ROTTAY IS THE RESULT THAT CHANGED: it went from 'the harness refuses the run, there is no arm' to an EQUIVALENT arm -- rottay/warm-sand and rottay/pale-mint, static moved=4 inert=848 and db moved=4 inert=848, both arms landing --ds-color-primary and --ds-chart-series-1 at the same values (#FFD166/#BD9114 and #A7F3D0/#5FAA8A), with producedBy.input.modeScope = 'dark', which is rottay's own default. bithire/crimson, bithire/indigo, evnto/crimson and evnto/indigo re-verify at 0 divergent rows under the R-2 code, modeScope 'light' -- the predicted no-op for the light-default verticals, confirmed rather than assumed. H-2 is PASS on BOTH arms in all six: the DB arm carries exactly two witnesses per vertical and publishes its three exclusions by id, the static arm carries five (it applies no contrast floor), and --ds-color-primary discriminates everywhere. RECEIPTED under the DT's per-vertical roster ruling of 2026-08-24. Artifacts and receipts: test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/F4B/palette-seeds/{rottay-warm-sand,rottay-pale-mint,bithire-crimson,bithire-indigo,evnto-crimson,evnto-indigo}.json plus the .receipt.json beside each, cited by calibration.staticDbParityEvidenceIds and calibration.exactRestoreEvidenceIds. unmeasuredScope: WHAT THE SIX RECEIPTS DO NOT COVER. The causal half IS measured and receipted -- painted equivalence, exact restore and the negative controls, in a browser, on both arms of all three verticals -- so the claim is no longer 'nothing is claimed' but the BOUNDED one in calibration.equivalenceClaimScope. What stays unmeasured is what that bound excludes: (a) the stops each vertical's DB door refuses -- crimson/indigo on rottay, warm-sand/pale-mint on bithire and evnto. Those stops DO lower on the static arm (it applies no contrast floor, which is why it carries five witnesses against the DB arm's two), so what is unmeasured there is not the lowering but the EQUIVALENCE: there is no DB counterpart to diff them against, and none is claimed; (b) the scene of a tenant document that declares NO backgroundMode, which on a dark-default vertical lands in modes.light and was named rather than measured (ROTTAY_DB_SEED_LANDS_IN_THE_NON_DEFAULT_MODE.openProductQuestion); and (c) the identity stop on the DB arm, which that arm cannot lower by law (W-A) and which therefore carries no equivalence claim.
NO FAMILY CELL IS WRITTEN. primitive/inputs/button remains the candidate; a cell would have to name evidence that does not exist.

THE PER-VERTICAL ROSTER IS A MEASURED FACT, NOT AN ADJUDICATED SHAPE. Whether a control may carry receipts whose admissible stop set differs per vertical is a DT ruling this packet raises and does not take.
The background/ground axis is unmeasured: step 0 proved it is not independently writable through the DB door.

The secondary and accent roles have no causal scenario. Their per-role isolation is drilled on the compiler, but the five declared channels are all primary-flavoured, so a secondary or accent stop emits none of them and cannot be a witness. Widening declaredOutputs is a REGISTRY change and was out of this packet.
The correctness of the OKLCH derivation itself -- perceptual evenness, no hue drift at step 700 -- has no home in negative-control-shaped machinery and is not claimed.

THE BLAST RADIUS OF ASYMMETRIC_CONTRAST_VALIDATION_BETWEEN_DOORS IS UNMEASURED. Whether controls other than this one are exposed to the static door's missing contrast floor was not measured; this control is where it was found.

assertStopDiscrimination still builds its witness vector from the BASE map only. Under the scope-matched ruling that is sound for this control (every admissible stop lands in the body), and the widening cannot turn a PASS into a FAIL because an added witness can only grow the value set. It was NOT widened, and the residual hazard is named rather than fixed: a control whose stops legitimately lived only in a mode block could read as constant there.

knownDefects.finding: MEASURED IN THE ARTIFACTS, not inferred. Each vertical artifact declares --ds-color-primary TWICE: at :is(html[data-tenant=X], :where([data-ds-root][data-vertical=X])) and again at that SAME selector plus [data-theme='dark'] (rottay: .light). bithire index.css:323 and :1371 are the two lines. The mode block carries one extra attribute, so it outranks the static arm's appended tenant block by SPECIFICITY — appending later does not help. The DB arm writes inline on the document element and is not outranked. Result: the static arm is structurally inert, in that mode, for every channel the artifact re-declares per mode. Accounts for all 7 dark rows on bithire and all 4 on evnto.
knownDefects.classNote: SUPERSEDED BY M-1, and the previous reading was WRONG rather than incomplete. It called this an instance of OPEN_VERTICAL_CASCADE_DEFECT owned by the vertical-artifact generator. M-1 measured the compilers and refuted that: the double declaration is the CORRECT OUTPUT of compileModeBlocks (a base block plus one block per authored non-default mode, under a one-attribute-stronger selector), and the two compilers AGREE in that mode — the tenant seed does not reach the overlay (bithire: base moves 22 channels, the dark block 0), and compileTenantThemeConfig even ADDS a dark delta re-asserting the vertical values (0 -> 29 vars) precisely to hold that line. The generator has no defect here. What was wrong was the INSTRUMENT: the static arm wrote only the base scope (fixed in M-1: it now emits 1+n blocks at the compiler's own themeModeSelector), and the DB arm still drops compiled modeDeltas and writes inline on the document element, where it outranks every mode block and produces a reading no production path produces. The remaining question — SHOULD a tenant seed move the non-default mode — is a PRODUCT adjudication, not a defect of this control.

knownDefects.finding: The color-set branch refuses any non-hex stop value. That is a restriction OF THE HARNESS, not of the product: the DB compiler accepts functional colour syntax (tenant-theme-compiler.test.ts:1187). What the branch refuses to do is lower a value whose downstream meaning it cannot predict on both arms — measured, a non-hex seed goes silently grey through the ramp derivation while the isHexColor-guarded channels skip entirely.

THE LAST THREE ROWS, and they are not a disagreement between compilers. On bithire in LIGHT, --ds-button-primary-bg reads #3A6FB0 on the static arm and var(--ds-color-primary) on the DB arm, which also moves the button background-color and border-top-color it paints. Measured cause: `applyTenantSeedDerivations` (kernel/runtime/brand-theme:1614) re-derives the primary family a TENANT seed owns, and it fires ONLY when `provenance.seedIsTenantAuthored`. bithire is the one vertical whose baseline bakes a literal colour at chrome.controls.buttonPrimary.bg (#3A6FB0; rottay and evnto author var(--ds-color-primary) and are therefore unaffected), and the rule replaces exactly that kind of value: "a BASELINE_LEAF cannot beat a TENANT_DERIVED value".
knownDefects.refutedExplanations: TWO were checked and BOTH are false. (a) A baseline divergence: the two transports do NOT receive different verticals -- the DB baseline is FIRST_PARTY_THEMES[verticalKey] = brandThemeToTheme(bithireBrandTheme), the same source the static arm composes over. (b) A compiler defect: it is the SAME lowering; `compileTheme` and `compileBrandTheme` live in one file and share `applyTenantSeedDerivations`.
knownDefects.decisiveExperiment: Same compiler, same theme, same patch, one variable changed: compileBrandTheme({brandTheme: bithire, tenantPatch: {palette:{primaryColor:"#DC2626"}}, tenantSlug:"bithire"}) emits --ds-button-primary-bg = #3A6FB0; adding tenantAuthoredPaths: Set(["palette.primaryColor"]) to the SAME call emits var(--ds-color-primary) -- byte-identical to the DB arm. The provenance flag alone explains the divergence.
knownDefects.adjudication: BRANCH (c): legitimate behaviour of two transports for two tenant classes, with the caveat that it is a PROBE FIDELITY GAP rather than a permanent product truth. The compiler contract says so in its own words: tenantAuthoredPaths is "supplied only for the tenant leg of a DB compile; a baseline compile supplies nothing and therefore compiles exactly as it did before provenance existed", and the rule's doc adds "every static first-party compile takes this path". So the DB arm is right, the static arm is right about a FIRST-PARTY compile, and the probe's static arm is modelling something in between: it lowers a TENANT patch (B-1) while compiling as a baseline.
knownDefects.answerToOptionB: YES -- under option B a tenant seed SHOULD move bithire's button, and the compiler already does exactly that on the transport that knows it is a tenant. The channel is a vertical chrome leaf, and `SEED_SHADOWING_FIELDS` names it: a TENANT leaf at that path would outrank the tenant's own seed, but bithire's #3A6FB0 is a BASELINE leaf and does not.

knownDefects.resolutionMeasured: CLOSED, measured on both bithire stops: 3 divergent rows -> 0, pass=true, restore exact, negatives held. The remediation this entry named is what landed, and it landed where the entry said it belonged -- in the instrument, with no compiler and no baseline touched.
knownDefects.adjudicationClauseAged: THE QUOTATION IN `adjudication` AGED, and B-2 corrected the source rather than the quote. It cited the compiler contract saying tenantAuthoredPaths is 'supplied only for the tenant leg of a DB compile'. That clause described the only producer that existed; the gate run before B-2 measured that baseline+patch is the ONLY composition production performs and that production never performs it WITHOUT a set, so an arm composing both floors silently was the defect, not the exception. The clause is amended at src/infrastructure/compilers/kernel/runtime/brand-theme/index.ts (compileTheme.tenantAuthoredPaths). The rest of the adjudication -- branch (c), the probe fidelity gap, and `answerToOptionB` -- stands unchanged and is what B-2 executed.

knownDefects.finding: MEASURED (R-1), and the hop that diverges is migrateV1 while the fact of data is ONE boolean: appearance.defaultMode. rottay is the only first-party vertical whose default mode is dark. A v1 tenant document that declares no palette.backgroundMode takes `?? "light"` (migrate-v1/index.ts:396) and its top-level seeds are routed to the LIGHT mode (:404-418) -- which on a light-default vertical is the Theme body, and on rottay is modes.light, an overlay. So the compiled artifact's base delta is legitimately empty while modeDeltas[light] carries the whole lowering: 19 variables, two of them declared. The static door has no such routing -- it writes palette.primaryColor into the BrandTheme body, i.e. the default mode -- so on rottay the two doors wrote different mode scopes and a parity run would have diffed two different questions.
knownDefects.instrumentHalf: THE REFUSAL WAS AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT, not a product one, and it had two sites of the same era. lowerStop's empty-lowering guard stood between the base extraction and the mode extraction H-3 phase (a) added 35 lines below it, so it asked 'is the base map empty?' and answered a question about the whole lowering; assertVariables (used by composeStaticArm/composeDbArm) had the same shape. R-2 moves the check below the mode extraction and asks it over the UNION of every scope the compiler wrote, in both sites. FAIL-CLOSED IS UNCHANGED WHERE IT MATTERS: an arm empty in the base map AND in every mode block is still refused, now with a message that names the scopes. The widening is monotone -- it only ADMITS lowerings the old law refused, and every receipted arm has a non-empty base map -- so no receipted arm is re-adjudicated (R-2 drill 7).
knownDefects.productHalf: THE SCOPE MISMATCH IS A CONTRACT FACT, and the probe now removes it by declaration rather than by hoping. DT ruling 2026-08-24: the probe's DB document declares backgroundMode = the vertical's own defaultMode, read fail-closed from the PUBLISHED BrandTheme in dist (<vertical>BrandTheme.appearance.defaultMode -- W-A). W-A's own reason for that source was REFUTED by the verification it asked for: it held that FIRST_PARTY_THEMES.<v>.appearance.defaultMode is undefined, and measured it is 'dark' -- the Theme projection DOES carry the field. The prescription stands for a stronger reason, asserted in R-2 drill 3: FIRST_PARTY_THEMES is not EXPORTED from the published entrypoint at all, so reaching it would take the deep import this harness refuses for its compilers, while <vertical>BrandTheme is published and already loaded. Measured after the change: on all three verticals the DB seed lands in the base map at the same value the static arm writes. The stamp is scoped to documents that already write a palette node -- see NON_PALETTE_DOCUMENTS_MUST_NOT_MATERIALISE_A_PALETTE_NODE.
knownDefects.openProductQuestion: NOT closed by this packet and owned by the owner, registered in the roadmap (DT rulings 6a): a REAL rottay tenant that writes only its palette, with no backgroundMode, still lands in modes.light -- branding that its product does not show by default. The probe's declaration models the dominant tenant intent for a parity run; it does not change what the transport does for a tenant who does not declare.

knownDefects.finding: MEASURED (R-1, reproduced by the preaudit and again in R-2): the two doors do not apply the same validation. compileTenantThemeConfig runs validateCompiledThemeContrast (tenant-theme/index.ts:1965) and REFUSES a tenant seed whose compiled pair falls below the governed APCA floor. compileBrandTheme has no contrast gate at all. So the static door emits exactly the pair the DB door rejects: on rottay, #DC2626 with on-primary ink #0C0C0E -- the same Lc 32.2 -- compiles silently. The consequence is visible in this control's own roster: all four colour stops lower on the static arm on all three verticals, while the DB arm admits only two per vertical.
knownDefects.scope: ALCANCE NO MEDIDO. Whether other controls are exposed to the same asymmetry was not measured; this control is where it was found.
knownDefects.owner: product question registered in the roadmap (DT rulings 6b), not a defect of this control

knownDefects.finding: MEASURED IN R-2, BEFORE THE CHANGE WAS WRITTEN, and it corrected the implementation. The scope-matched ruling reads 'the probe's DB document declares backgroundMode ALWAYS'; taken as 'on every document', it is unsafe. backgroundMode lives INSIDE palette, so writing it into a document that has no palette node MATERIALISES one. migratePalette then returns a palette patch whose ten seed fields are all undefined, and collectPatchAuthoredPaths collects those ten as AUTHORED keypaths -- including palette.primaryColor, a member of CONSULTED_PROVENANCE_FIELDS. The compiler is thereby told a tenant selected a seed nobody wrote, the governed seed-derivation ladder fires, and channels repaint. Measured: 24 of the 36 receipted DB-arm compiles change VALUE that way (density.mode, spacing.rhythm, surfaces.effect-intensity and experience.profile, on all three verticals), with --ds-button-primary-bg, --ds-button-primary-bg-hover and --ds-color-border-focus among the new rows. That also falsifies the ruling's own justification, which says 'in bithire/evnto nothing changes'.
knownDefects.resolution: The stamp is scoped to documents that already write a palette node, which is the reading under which the ruling's stated consequence is true. Every control whose door is not a palette keypath builds a byte-identical document to the one it built before R-2. Fenced by R-2 drill 4, which asserts both halves: a palette door with no declared scope fails closed, and a spacing.rhythm document comes out as exactly { rhythm: 'airy' }.

calibration.stopAdmissibilityByVertical: MEASURED IN R-2, and it is a PARTITION rather than a shortlist. Under the scope-matched ruling the DB document declares backgroundMode = the vertical's own defaultMode, so the governed contrast floor is evaluated against that mode's on-primary ink -- which is #0C0C0E on rottay (dark default) and #ffffff on bithire/evnto (light default). A near-black ink demands a LIGHT seed; a white ink demands a DARK one. Measured over a 216-seed sweep of the RGB cube: ZERO seeds are admissible on all three verticals, 79 are rottay-only, 122 are bithire+evnto-only, 15 are admissible nowhere, and the mixed-other bucket is EMPTY -- bithire and evnto always agree with each other and always disagree with rottay. So the roster is per-vertical by construction, not by preference. DB arm: primary/crimson (#DC2626) and primary/indigo (#4F46E5) lower on bithire and evnto and are REFUSED on rottay (APCA Lc 32.2 and 23.2, dark --ds-button-primary-color against --ds-button-primary-bg); primary/warm-sand (#FFD166) and primary/pale-mint (#A7F3D0) lower on rottay and are REFUSED on bithire and evnto (Lc -23.9 and -16.1, light, same pair). Each vertical therefore has exactly TWO DB witnesses, which is what keeps H-2 decidable per arm. STATIC arm: all four lower on all three, because compileBrandTheme has no contrast floor at all -- see ASYMMETRIC_CONTRAST_VALIDATION_BETWEEN_DOORS. primary/identity is a static-arm claim (W-B) and lowers on neither DB vertical: it emits 7 variables and none of the five declared channels.
calibration.modeScopeRecord: WHERE THE SCOPE IS ON THE RECORD, named once so a reader does not excavate it. (i) producedBy.input.modeScope -- the backgroundMode the DB document declared for this run, or null on the static arm and on any DB document with no palette node. (ii) producedBy.input.compilerInput.appearance.palette.backgroundMode -- the same value where it physically travels, inside the input actually handed to compile(). It is NOT in producedBy.input.document, which is the manifest-path-relative shape buildIngressInput built before toCompilerInput reshaped it; W-A asked for this to be verified rather than assumed, and it was (R-2 drill 3). (iii) producedBy.modeChannels -- the per-channel scope census M-1 already emitted: which modes the compiler wrote a block for and which declared channels each one carries. That is the record that tells 'this control has nothing in any mode block' apart from 'this control is governed per mode', and after R-2 it is also what makes an empty base map readable instead of alarming.
calibration.equivalenceClaimScope: THE CLAIM THIS CONTROL MAKES, BOUNDED, AND IT IS NOT 'THE TWO DOORS ARE EQUIVALENT'. What is verified is: EQUIVALENCE FOR THE STOPS ADMISSIBLE ON EACH VERTICAL, UNDER AN EXPLICIT modeScope EQUAL TO THAT VERTICAL'S DEFAULT MODE. Three bounds, each measured rather than assumed. (i) STOPS: only two of the four declared colour stops are admissible per vertical, and the sets are complementary (calibration.stopAdmissibilityByVertical); nothing is claimed for the stops each vertical's contrast floor refuses, and nothing at all is claimed for the identity stop on the DB arm. (ii) SCOPE: every run declares palette.backgroundMode = the vertical's own defaultMode (producedBy.input.modeScope), which is what puts both doors in the same mode in the first place. A tenant document that declares NO backgroundMode is a different scene -- on a dark-default vertical the seed lands in modes.light -- and this control measured that scene only to the extent of naming it (ROTTAY_DB_SEED_LANDS_IN_THE_NON_DEFAULT_MODE.openProductQuestion). (iii) CHANNELS: the equivalence is over the painted diff of the measured fixture roster; three of the five declared channels cannot witness on some vertical for structural reasons (measuredResult.r2BlindWitnesses). THE DOORS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC AND THIS CONTROL SAYS SO: the DB door applies a governed contrast floor that the static door does not have at all, which is why the static arm lowers five witness stops where the DB arm lowers two (ASYMMETRIC_CONTRAST_VALIDATION_BETWEEN_DOORS). A reader may cite these six receipts for the bounded claim above and for nothing wider.
